Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: The _____ was Library at the Institute of France in Paris.
Bibliothèque Mazarine.fact: The Bibliothèque Mazarine, or Mazarin Library, is located within the Palais de l'institut de France, or the Palace of the Institute of France (previously the Collège des Quatre-Nations of the University of Paris), at 23 quai de Conti in the 6th arrondissement, on the Left Bank of the Seine facing the Pont des Arts and the Louvre.

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: He went into the church and studied at the _____ in Rome, though he declined to join their order

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: He went into the Papal service, where he became known for his diplomatic, political and military skills, and was assigned as a nuncio to the French court from _____ to 1636
Bibliothèque Mazarine.fact: He went into the Papal service, where he became known for his diplomatic, political and military skills, and was assigned as a nuncio to the French court from 1634 to 1636.

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: His talents brought him to the elder _____, the chief minister of Louis XIII, who made him a member of the council of State of the King
Bibliothèque Mazarine.fact: His talents brought him to the elder Cardinal Richelieu, the chief minister of Louis XIII, who made him a member of the council of State of the King.

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: When he came from Rome to Paris, he brought with him a library of five thousand books which he had kept in his palace on the _____ in Rome
Bibliothèque Mazarine.fact: When he came from Rome to Paris, he brought with him a library of five thousand books which he had kept in his palace on the Quirinal Hill in Rome.

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: With the death of Louis XIII in _____, Mazarin became the new Prime Minister, with the support of the Queen, Anne of Austria
Bibliothèque Mazarine.fact: With the death of Louis XIII in 1643, Mazarin became the new Prime Minister, with the support of the Queen, Anne of Austria.

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: He immediately began constructing a palace for himself on rue de _____ in Paris, with an enormous chamber fifty-eight meters long designed especially to house his library
Bibliothèque Mazarine.fact: His talents brought him to the elder Cardinal Richelieu, the chief minister of Louis XIII, who made him a member of the council of State of the King. He immediately began constructing a palace for himself on rue de Richelieu in Paris, with an enormous chamber fifty-eight meters long designed especially to house his library.

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: Visitors, including _____ III, the King of Denmark, came from around Europe to see his library, and to model their own royal libraries after his
Bibliothèque Mazarine.fact: Visitors, including Frederick III, the King of Denmark, came from around Europe to see his library, and to model their own royal libraries after his.

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: The library nearly came to an end in January and February _____ with the outbreak of the Fronde, an uprising by several powerful nobles against the authority of Mazarin
Bibliothèque Mazarine.fact: The library nearly came to an end in January and February 1652 with the outbreak of the Fronde, an uprising by several powerful nobles against the authority of Mazarin.

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: Mazarin and the young _____ were forced to flee Paris
Bibliothèque Mazarine.fact: Visitors, including Frederick III, the King of Denmark, came from around Europe to see his library, and to model their own royal libraries after his. Between 1642 and 1653, Mazarin's librarian, Gabriel Naudé, traveled to Italy, Switzerland, Germany, England and Holand, buying entire libraries for Mazarin's collection, making it the largest library in Europe at the time, with forty thousand volumes.

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: When Mazarin was finally able to return to Paris and to power in _____, Naudé was able to get back many of the books which had been sold or stolen
Bibliothèque Mazarine.fact: When Mazarin was finally able to return to Paris and to power in 1653, Naudé was able to get back many of the books which had been sold or stolen.

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: Mazarin then began a second library with what was left of the first, assisted by the successor to Naudé, François de _____
Bibliothèque Mazarine.fact: Mazarin then began a second library with what was left of the first, assisted by the successor to Naudé, François de La Poterie.

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: Since _____, Mazarin had opened his library to scholars
Bibliothèque Mazarine.fact: Since 1643, Mazarin had opened his library to scholars.

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: It was open on _____, and each week some eighty to one hundred came to do research
Bibliothèque Mazarine.fact: It was open on Thursdays, and each week some eighty to one hundred came to do research.

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: The collection was matched by only three other libraries in Europe: the _____ of Oxford; the Ambrosian Library in Milan and the Angelique Library in Rome
Bibliothèque Mazarine.fact: The collection was matched by only three other libraries in Europe: the Bodleian Library of Oxford; the Ambrosian Library in Milan and the Angelique Library in Rome.

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: After his experience with the Fronde, _____ wanted to assure that his library remained intact after his death
Bibliothèque Mazarine.fact: After his experience with the Fronde, Mazarin wanted to assure that his library remained intact after his death. On the fronton is the inscription in Latin: Bibliotheca a fundatore mazarinea (Library set up by Mazarin).

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: The new library building was constructed on the exact site of the medieval Tour de Nesle, or _____, on the banks of the Seine

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: On the fronton is the inscription in Latin: _____ a fundatore mazarinea (Library founded by Mazarin)
Bibliothèque Mazarine.fact: On the fronton is the inscription in Latin: Bibliotheca a fundatore mazarinea (Library set up by Mazarin).

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: The new library opened for Easter in _____

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: The library continued to grow during the 18th century, from 36,000 volumes in _____ to 50,000 in 1771

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: He also collected works of art, mostly from the 17th and 18th centuries, gilded bronze chandeliers, Louis XVI commodes, a globe of the heavens by Gastellier from _____, and other objects which decorat

Bibliothèque Mazarine.fact: In 1805, under Napoleon I, The Collège des Quatre-Nations became the Palace of the Institut de France, the headquarters of the French scholarly and scientific academies.

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: Since that time the Library has received donations of numerous large collections, and since _____ has also been the depository of publications relating to the history of the regions of France

Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: The oldest part of the collection, brought together by _____, contains about 200,000 volumes on all subjects

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Bibliothèque Mazarine.question: Other specialities are the history of the book and the local and regional history of _____

Bibliothèque Mazarine.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
